sections.title: Form and cultivation
sections.text: A tall ornamental mallow, often grown as a biennial or short-lived perennial; Kew treats its origin as a cultigen from Türkiye. Its upright flowering spike is commonly 1.5–2.4 m tall and carries large cup- or funnel-shaped flowers. Alternate rounded, lobed leaves become smaller up the stem. The dry fruit separates into seed-bearing segments.

sections.title: Food and distinction
sections.text: The flowers are listed as edible garnish by horticultural sources. The sources consulted do not establish human toxicity. Hollyhock is a garden ornamental and should not be confused with marsh mallow (Althaea officinalis).
